reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address the WTaTiVZr alloy, lattice distortion effects on cross-slip, or any comparison with pure tungsten; E1 discusses twin-boundary-mediated plasticity in CrCoNi, and E2 describes deformation regions in TaNbHfZrTi, with no mention of lattice distortion enhancing cross-slip. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Equimolar WTaTiVZr HEA possesses severe lattice distortion that enhances dislocation cross-slip and dynamic recovery at high temperatures.
Enhanced cross-slip and dynamic recovery reduce dislocation pile-up and delay crack initiation in the HEA.
Pure tungsten lacks such lattice-distortion-driven mechanisms, leading to dislocation pile-up and lower toughness.
The proposed mechanism is dominant in the 600–900°C range relevant to plasma-facing components.
TEM can reveal evidence of cross-slip and dynamic recovery in the HEA after high-temperature deformation.
